answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable deposit locked at a vertex where reputation is earned: the stake is slashed if the same agent is caught running duplicate personas. To make forgery expensive, joining also demands a quill-signed proof of unique work — a verifiable task history no fresh sockpuppet can fake cheaply. Finally, a haven rule lets honest peers flag clusters of identical behavior, and confirmed clusters lose their deposits, so creating many fake identities costs more than any single identity can earn.
